s1.syndrome_frame: Acute pruritic skin eruption with vesicles and erythema following sun exposure
salient_findings: Numerous small blisters on ears and vermillion border
Erythematous papules and crusts on cheeks, neck, and lower arms
key_facts: 13-year-old boy presented with skin eruption
Eruption appeared 24 hours after intensive sun exposure
Patient had episode of malaise and headache 2 weeks before presentation
No history of photosensitivity
No use of topical or systemic photosensitizers
Laboratory tests showed detectable serum parvovirus B19 IgM and IgG antibodies
PVB19 DNA found in lesional skin biopsy specimen
Standard phototesting with UV-A and UV-B was unremarkable
Patient had helical thickening and erythema on ears
Crusted papules and small erosions on cheeks

shortlist.label: Parvovirus B19-associated erythema
shortlist.why_kept: Detectable serum parvovirus B19 IgM and IgG antibodies and PVB19 DNA found in lesional skin biopsy specimen

shortlist.label: Polymorphic light eruption
shortlist.why_kept: Acute pruritic skin eruption with vesicles and erythema following sun exposure

shortlist.label: Erythema multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: Skin eruption with helical thickening, erythema, and numerous small vesicles

shortlist.label: Phototoxic reaction
shortlist.why_kept: Skin eruption appeared 24 hours after intensive sun exposure

shortlist.label: Hydroa vacciniforme
shortlist.why_kept: Skin eruption with vesicles and erythema on sun-exposed areas

raw.rationale: The presence of detectable serum parvovirus B19 IgM and IgG antibodies and PVB19 DNA in the lesional skin biopsy specimen, along with the patient's symptoms and lack of history of photosensitivity, supports this diagnosis

rejected.label: Polymorphic light eruption
rejected.why: While the eruption appeared after sun exposure, the presence of PVB19 DNA and antibodies points more specifically to a viral etiology

rejected.label: Erythema multiforme
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and laboratory findings do not specifically align with the typical target lesions and lack of viral DNA in lesional skin seen in erythema multiforme

rejected.label: Phototoxic reaction
rejected.why: The patient had no history of using photosensitizers and standard phototesting was unremarkable, making this less likely

rejected.label: Hydroa vacciniforme
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and the specific finding of PVB19 DNA in lesional skin do not align with hydroa vacciniforme, which typically presents with more severe scarring and is associated with Epstein-Barr virus
